summary: Jerry Liu presents on building AI agents that automate knowledge work, noting that 90% of enterprise data exists as unstructured documents. He distinguishes two UX categories: assistive agents with chat interfaces, unconstrained ReAct-style architectures, and high human-in-the-loop guidance; and automation agents that run in the background, use more constrained architectures to avoid going off the rails, process batch inputs, and output structured results with batch review rather than step-by-step oversight. The stack has two pillars: really good tools (enabled by protocols like MCP) and agent architectures encoding business logic. The document toolbox generalizes beyond naive RAG, requiring data connectors, document parsing/extraction, indexing into vector/SQL/graph stores, and tool interfaces for semantic search, file lookup, manipulation, and structured querying. Complex documents—PDFs with embedded tables, charts, irregular layouts—require combining LLMs, LVMs, traditional parsing, and test-time agentic validation to outperform existing benchmarks. LlamaIndex's new Excel agent handles unnormalized spreadsheets that RAG and text-to-CSV cannot process, using reinforcement learning to learn a semantic map of the sheet, achieving 95% accuracy versus 70-75% code-interpreter baselines and 90% human baselines. A key architectural pattern emerges: automation agents serve as backends processing and structuring data, while assistant agents serve as front-end user-facing interfaces consuming those structured tools. Real-world use cases include Carl's financial due diligence platform combining automation (ingesting unstructured financial data with human review) and assistant (co-pilot for analysts) UXs; SEMX's enterprise search with agentic RAG chatbots over multiple data collections; and a global electronics company's technical data sheet injection automation that encodes business-specific parsing logic, transforming weeks of manual technical writer work into automated extraction with SQL output. LlamaIndex positions itself as the most accurate customizable platform for automating document workflows with agentic AI.

sections.title: Introduction and Knowledge Work Automation Promise
sections.summary: Jerry Liu introduces himself and the topic of building AI agents that automate knowledge work. He questions whether knowledge work automation just means building RAG chatbots and outlines that 90% of enterprise data is unstructured documents requiring AI agents to reason and act over them.

sections.title: Agent Categories and Stack Components
sections.summary: Defines two agent categories: assistive agents (chat interface, human-in-the-loop) and automation agents (background, routine tasks). The stack requires two components: good tools and agent architecture. Outlines three talk topics: document toolbox, agent design patterns, and document agent use cases.

sections.title: Building a Document Toolbox
sections.summary: Introduces the document toolbox as a generalization beyond naive RAG. Requires a pre-processing layer with data connectors, document parsing/extraction, and indexing into vector/SQL/graph stores. Defines the document MCP server concept with tools for semantic search, file lookup, manipulation, and structured querying.

sections.title: Complex Documents and LLM/LVM-Based Parsing
sections.summary: Addresses the challenge of complex documents with embedded tables, charts, and irregular layouts designed for human consumption. LlamaIndex combines LLMs and LVMs with traditional parsing and test-time agentic validation, outperforming existing parsing benchmarks using Sonnet 3.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and GPT-4.1.

sections.title: LlamaIndex Platform and Excel Agent Capabilities
sections.summary: Announces new Excel agent capabilities that handle unnormalized spreadsheets, which RAG and text-to-CSV cannot process. Uses reinforcement learning to learn a semantic map of the sheet, translating it into specialized tools. Achieves 95% accuracy versus 70-75% code-interpreter baseline and 90% human baseline on synthetic Excel data.

sections.title: Agent Orchestration Spectrum
sections.summary: Introduces the agent orchestration spectrum from constrained architectures with explicit control flow to unconstrained architectures like ReAct, function calling, and CodeAct. Sets up the transition to discussing agent design patterns and document agent use cases.

sections.title: Assistive vs Automation UX Architectures
sections.summary: Details the two UX categories. Assistive UXs are chat-oriented with natural language input, unconstrained ReAct-loop architectures, and high human-in-the-loop guidance. Automation UXs take batch inputs, run in the background or ad hoc, use more constrained architectures to avoid going off rails, have less human-in-the-loop with batch review, and output structured results routed to downstream systems. Use cases include financial data normalization, data sheet extraction, invoice reconciliation, and contract review. References the open-source invoice reconciler by Lori Boss.

sections.title: Automation-as-Backend Pattern
sections.summary: Describes an emerging pattern where automation agents serve as backends running in the background doing data ETL and transformation with some human-in-the-loop, while assistant agents are front-end facing. Automation agents process and structure data and provide tool interfaces for assistant agents serving research or user-facing interfaces.

sections.title: Real-World Document Agent Use Cases
sections.summary: Presents three real-world use cases. Carl combines automation and assistant UXs for financial due diligence: automation ingests unstructured financial data (Excel, PDFs, PowerPoints) with bespoke extraction and human review, then a co-pilot interface helps analysts get insights and generate reports. SEMX uses assistant UX for enterprise search with agentic RAG chatbots over multiple data collections. A global electronics company uses pure automation for technical data sheet injection, encoding business-specific parsing logic, extracting information, matching rules, and outputting structured data to SQL, transforming weeks of manual technical writer work into automated extraction.

sections.title: LlamaIndex Positioning and Closing
sections.summary: Liu closes by positioning LlamaIndex as the most accurate customizable platform for automating document workflows with agentic AI, noting the mission has evolved from a broad horizontal RAG framework. Invites attendees to visit Booth G11.
